title: Pass over an item that fails twice while flagged, don't stop batch
summary: Extends the earlier fix (a batch no longer stops on repeated failure of an item whose line the scope guard paused) to lines the guard only flagged (T1/T3/T5), as for item 20261103-193428-df2m. After two failed attempts on a flagged line, the drain passes the item over with a reason and runs the next item; the audience is the operator running `athena drain` batches. Previous job 20261103-193428-df2m (a different fix, job-slot counting) is related by id only, so its work is not carried here.

defaults_applied.how: Change and test in Rust under crates/athena-cli.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check must pass.
A drain test exercises two failures on a flagged line then the next item running.
The stop decision at the ATTEMPTS failure point in Drain::attempts is changed for flagged lines, not just this item.
One focused change in drain.rs and its tests, plus a changelog line.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (Drain::attempts around lines 1735-1830, where failures >= ATTEMPTS returns ItemEnd::Failed unless paused_reason finds a pause; Steps::paused at ~650; RealSteps::paused at ~3339) and crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs (Athena::line_pause at 782 returns only Level::Pause marks; live_marks at 796 also holds flags). The cause: line_pause ignores flags, so a flagged line that fails twice yields ItemEnd::Failed and the repeated-failure stop. No record or data file is added, so the records allow-list is untouched; the property is measured by driving Drain with stub Steps in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs.

Reading of 'pause it': after the second failure on a flagged line the drain passes the item over for the rest of the batch (as ItemEnd::Paused does today), with a note naming the flag signals; it does not write a new pause file. Simplest route: a new defaulted Steps method (e.g. flagged) backed by Athena::live_marks, consulted at the ATTEMPTS point alongside paused_reason.
The earlier landed fix's tests in tests/drain.rs for paused lines stay passing; an unflagged, unpaused item failing twice still stops the batch as 'repeated failure'.

Job 20261103-193428-df2m is only the example incident (the item flagged T1, T3, T5); its own verification findings (uncited command evidence for a behavior criterion) concern a different change and are addressed here by naming runnable commands in each behavior criterion.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs: an item fails twice on a line that is flagged (not paused), and the batch then runs the next item, which is recorded as run/landed, with no 'repeated failure' stop. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and see it pass.
A test shows an item that fails twice with no flag and no pause still ends the batch with the repeated-failure stop naming it. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.

The passed-over flagged item is reported with a line naming it and its flag reason, and the batch summary does not count it as a failed item stopping the run. Checked by the new test's assertions on output under `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
Existing paused-line drain tests still pass; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

drain.rs (Drain::attempts, the stop-reasons text and the module docs near line 26 and 944) says a line that is flagged or paused is passed over after two failures; Grep for 'flagged' in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs shows the new rule documented where the old paused rule is.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that a batch no longer stops on repeated failure of a flagged item, citing the 3 Nov incident with item 20261103-193428-df2m.

out_of_scope: Job 20261103-193428-df2m's change (re-read 'needs accepting' not counting toward --job-limit): not kept or redone here; its files drain.rs, tests/drain.rs, main.rs and CHANGELOG.md are only touched here for this request's change, and its 'needs accepting' slot logic is not part of this job.
Changing the scope guard's T1-T5 thresholds or when a flag or pause is recorded.
Changing the stop on repeated failure for items whose line is neither flagged nor paused.
Writing or lifting pause files on disk beyond what the existing watcher already does.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow files.
hard_reason: Changes a rule that decides whether a batch stops (the drain's repeated-failure stop), part of the run pipeline.
